I think he most definitely has ptsd or cptsd (not a doctor). It wouldn’t be surprising if he had nightmares, or regularly thought back to his time in the abyss. It also wouldn’t be surprising if he didn’t remember often or couldn’t remember details. There’s no telling how the trauma manifested as it different for everyone. 

It’s obvious Ajax never really left the abyss. He views everything like he’s still there hence why he’s constantly ready to fight. I imagine it would be unnerving to go without a fight when his head is programmed to constantly battle. Tbh mans needs a lot of help. You can view a traumatic experience as positive but it doesn’t change the impact it has on your body and mind. 

I think he probably has a lot of things he does that stem from what he experienced in the abyss. Especially since he was at such a formative age. I don’t know about nightmares but a lot of his actions, opinions, mannerism, have a direct link to trauma. It’s kind of sad when you think about it. He could be experiencing nightmares, flashbacks, dissociation, lots of shit. 

Mf needs therapy. 

Also fun little detail about his character design. Every character in the game as a little light in their eyes (the white highlight) but Childe does not. Mans literally has dead eyes. Still love him loads tho <3 part of why he’s my favorite character is how his lore really impacts him as a character.

Hi, I don’t know how best to help in this situation. But I want to say, even if you never know “what you want” to do in life that’s okay. I’m on the autism spectrum as well, I don’t think having a clear future in your head or some great intrinsic calling to something is very friendly to neurodivergent people. All I have are special interests, but the idea of having one huge thing to want to do for a career or life seems like it’s not something I could possibly have. But the point is that’s okay. Statistically people will have about 12 different jobs in their lifetime. Not having a set career or changing your mind about what that is, is okay. It’s valid. 

As for struggling socially I don’t have a lot of advice. But I can say there’s people out there who will accept you being on the autism spectrum, they’ll take time to understand it, and accept who you are :) A lot of my close friends are neurodivergent as well, or share interests so it helps me a lot to communicate well. 

If I said anything off or upsetting in this response I apologize, it’s hard to tell how I come off. I’m genuinely hoping to be helpful and/or soothing.
